articleTitle: System safety: Success factors in critical systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: The presentation draws on the authors' wide experience as Independent Safety Assessors (ISAs) to identify examples of both good and bad practice in the safety management of rail systems engineering projects. It explores some of the main challenges that projects encounter, and draws out guidance to help projects to overcome these challenges.

articleTitle: System engineering the extended East London Line
publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: The term systems engineering is used to define a systematic way to undertake projects. There is much theory about the use of systems engineering, which from the author's experience has not been well applied to rail projects. The talk considers a major rail project, the East London Line Project, which is now under construction. In particular the application of the principles of system engineering in a practical and pragmatic manner during the project definition phase will be discussed, and how this will be taken forward through the delivery phase into public service

publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: System Engineering has recognised role in avoiding costly integration and performance issues from occurring late in the project lifecycle. These benefits can often be difficult to quantify and can have a long payback period for a large project. There are however a number of tangible early gains that can be made from taking a systems approach from the outset both to the system and the organisation that delivers the system. This talk covers the experience to date of a project in progress.

articleTitle: The Jubilee and Northern Lines Upgrade Project - delivering increased safety and performance to the underground
publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: Over the coming years Tube Lines' Jubilee and Northern Lines Upgrade Project (JNUP) will be replacing the fixed-block trip-cock protected signalling and control system currently used on these lines with a transmission based moving block train control system aimed at improving the operational safety and performance of the underground system. Passengers using the Jubilee Line are already benefiting from increased capacity provided by a 7th car recently added to the rolling stock. In conjunction with the new train control system a number of additional enhancements that are also to be delivered as a part of the JNUP are intended to further reduce the constraints of the existing system and increase the performance of the rolling stock, offering an improvement in the overall journey time capability made available to London Underground. As far as possible, these changes will be implemented “behind the scenes” from a passenger's perspective, with minimal disruption to normal service operation. This presentation will provide an outline of the way in which the systems and safety engineering are being undertaken on the JNUP, taking into account the scale of the challenges faced.

articleTitle: Adapting universal principles of systems engineering to the specific needs of rail
publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: The presenter believes that railway systems engineering has the same principles as systems engineering in other fields but that the specific needs of rail sometimes require that these principles should be applied in a different way in rail compared with other sectors. The presentation will describe an activity to identify a set of universal principles of systems engineering. It will then describe case studies of the successful application of these principles in rail projects.

publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: Systems are increasingly dominated by Information Systems whose behaviour may be significantly influence by data (and data errors). This presentation describes the major systems issues arising out of a reliance on data and provides possible solutions for the justification of ‘fit-for-purpose’ of these systems.

articleTitle: Safety approval for new trains - is it reducing safety?
publicationTitle: 2006 Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on Systems Engineering in the Railways
abstract: In this paper, the author describes the difficulties faced by Hitachi in obtaining all necessary statutory and regulatory safety approvals for the new Class 395 CTRL Domestic Services EMU (“Project Javelin”). The current rolling stock safety approvals process is detailed together with the complex, numerous and often conflicting requirements of the approvals stakeholders. Finally, the author describes his own personal opinions on how the system could be streamlined without compromising safety.
